test_title: PYST 36 - SSC CHSL 2025 - General Awareness (Held On: 26 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Canada?

options.text: Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court

solution:
The correct answer is __**Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**: This feature was borrowed from the **Canadian Constitution**. Under Article 143 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or matters of public importance. This advisory role strengthens the judiciary's role in governance. 
• The **Canadian model of federalism** also influenced the Indian Constitution in other ways, such as the division of powers between the Union and States. 
• The advisory jurisdiction provides a mechanism for resolving legal uncertainties, ensuring clarity on constitutional or legal matters. This is a hallmark of the federal structure influenced by Canada. 
• None of the other options listed (Rule of Law, Impeachment of the President, Fundamental Duties) were borrowed from Canada. These features have their origins in other sources like the British Constitution, U.S. Constitution, or Soviet principles. 
• This distinctive feature in India ensures the Supreme Court’s role in offering legal counsel to the executive, promoting democratic accountability and rule of law. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction in Canada:** 
• The Canadian Supreme Court has a similar advisory jurisdiction, where the government can refer legal or constitutional questions to the court for its opinion. 
• This feature was adapted in India to ensure a consultative relationship between the judiciary and the executive. 
• **Article 143 of the Indian Constitution:** 
• This article empowers the President of India to refer questions of law or public importance to the Supreme Court. 
• The opinion provided by the Supreme Court under this article is advisory and not binding on the President. 
• Example: Presidential references like the **Keshav Singh case** or the **Babri Masjid demolition** are significant applications of this provision. 
• **Other Features Borrowed from Canada:** 
• **Federal system with a strong Centre:** The Indian Constitution follows a federal structure with a tilt towards central authority, inspired by Canada. 
• **Residuary Powers:** In India, the residuary powers (those not mentioned in the Union or State List) are vested with the Centre, similar to the Canadian model. 
• **Origins of Other Options:** 
• **Rule of Law:** Borrowed from the British Constitution, it signifies equality before the law and supremacy of law. 
• **Impeachment of the President:** Inspired by the U.S. Constitution, this process ensures checks and balances in a democracy. 
• **Fundamental Duties:** These were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, and were inspired by the Soviet Constitution. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Federal Features of Indian Constitution:** 
• India’s Constitution is federal in structure but unitary in spirit, influenced by the Canadian model. 
• Examples include division of powers, independent judiciary, and dual government system. 
• However, India has unique features like a single citizenship and flexibility in amending the Constitution, differentiating it from traditional federal states. 
• **Presidential Reference:** 
• One of the notable cases under Article 143 was the **Keshavananda Bharati case**, where basic structure doctrine was established. 
• Another example is the reference on the **Ayodhya land dispute** (2019).
